summary: Session-6 backend features fully verified: 8/8 pass in /app/backend/tests/test_babybabel_session6.py, plus session-5 regression 10/10 and session-4 regression 18/18 (36/36 total). Coverage: (A) housing_offered on POST /api/bookings — (a1) non-au-pair booking with housing_offered='private room' returns Booking.housing_offered='' (server discards it via `(body.housing_offered or '').strip() if au_pair else ''`), also verified via GET /api/bookings/{id}; (a2) au-pair booking (is_au_pair=true, lessons_count=30, housing_offered='Private ensuite, meals included, one friendly dog') round-trips the exact string on POST response, GET /api/bookings/{id}, AND GET /api/bookings/me; (a3) housing_offered='x'*801 returns 422 (Pydantic max_length=800); (a4) housing_offered key omitted → 200 with default ''. (B) Morning-of reminder in _generate_dynamic_notifications — (b1) paid booking today at now+4h yields exactly one morning:<booking_id> notification with title 'Session today at HH:MM' and body containing tutor name 'Sofía García'; a second GET /api/notifications does NOT create a duplicate (dedupe guard on kind holds); (b2) booking on now+3d+2h → no morning: notif (same_day guard); (b3) booking 15 min in the past → no morning: notif (delta_min > 10 guard); (b4) paid booking at now+60min yields BOTH morning:<id> (once) AND reminder:<id> (once) — the 2h reminder logic still fires unchanged alongside the new morning-of.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:919 — `(body.housing_offered or '').strip() if au_pair else ''` correctly discards housing_offered for non-au-pair bookings. Consider whether silently discarding vs returning a 400/warning better serves UX: a parent who fills housing while forgetting to toggle au-pair loses data without feedback. Non-blocking.

server.py:1430-1439 — morning-of guard `same_day and 10 < delta_min < 24*60`: the upper bound (24*60) is redundant since same_day already implies delta_min < 24h. The 10-min lower bound correctly excludes past/imminent bookings. Dedupe via `find_one({user_id, kind: 'morning:<id>'})` before insert works — same race concern as the review notif (two concurrent GETs could both see missing key and both insert), but a follow-up `find_one` on the exact key is idempotent enough for MVP. Consider a unique index on (user_id, kind) collection-wide.

server.py:1441 — 2-hour reminder uses `-30 < delta_min < 120` overlapping the morning-of window (both fire when the session is <2h away). Product intent is likely: both, to nudge twice. Verified in test_b4.

server.py:350 — `housing_offered: Optional[str] = Field(default='', max_length=800)` — Pydantic correctly enforces the 800-char cap and defaults to ''. No whitespace stripping on the input, but line 919 strips before persist. Slightly inconsistent: an 800-char string with trailing whitespace passes validation, then gets trimmed. Non-blocking.
server.py is now 1587 lines — splitting into routers (bookings/notifications/reviews/tutors/messages) is overdue but still non-blocking.

rca_of_issue: No open bugs found in this session. Note for future reference: the morning-of notification key format is `morning:<booking_id>`, mirroring `reminder:<booking_id>` and `review:<booking_id>`. The dedupe guard reads `db.notifications.find_one({user_id, kind: key})` before insert, so a second GET /notifications on the same booking is a no-op. Concurrent GETs from the same user could theoretically double-insert (read-race), but no unique index enforces this at the DB level; recommend `(user_id, kind)` unique index if this becomes a support issue.
